Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation: test motif translations when the grid visually consists of noisy background plus one seed object.
3. Use a small script to enumerate translations and construct output grids when manual scanning is error-prone. Validate by matching all demonstrated changed/unchanged cells; account for seed shape, legal translations within bounds, and any rotation/reflection only if supported by demonstrations.

Use demonstrations to identify which in-tile feature or count determines the output; do not assume every unusual cell or single marker is positive. 5. For sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field, identify the invariant of their parallel lines: constant row−column for down-right diagonals, or row+column for down-left diagonals. Demonstrations may show that the output fills the whole grid with a periodic color sequence indexed by that invariant. 8. Reply with only the action JSON object and do not call unrelated tools.
